name: Mega growth and retention
tagline: Support growth. Keep the length you grow.
image_alt: A woman with long dark curly hair, in profile, holds the ends of a curl between her fingers.
description: Why length does not seem to stick, an eight-week routine for scalp care and length retention, and what to look for on a label.
intro: Hair grows at the scalp, at roughly half an inch a month. You cannot hurry that along much. What you can change is how much of it survives to stay on your head. This plan works on both ends: scalp care, and keeping the hair you already have.

causes.title: Why length does not seem to stick
causes.intro: If your hair seems to stay the same length for years, it is usually not that it stopped growing. It is that the ends are breaking off about as fast as the roots come in.
items: Your ends are the oldest hair
The hair at your ends has been through every wash, every style and every bad day since it grew.
It has had years of wear, so it is always the first to go.
Dry hair is brittle hair, and brittle hair snaps instead of bending.
Curly and coily hair is drier by nature, because the oil from your scalp struggles to travel down a bend.
Detangling in a rush, combing dry, pulling through knots, restyling every day.
Most breakage happens in your hands, not in the bottle.
They change the hair fiber itself, and that does not wash out or grow back.
Cotton pillowcases and anything tight you sleep in.
Eight hours of rubbing, every night, adds up faster than anything you do in the day.
A scalp you have stopped noticing
New hair comes out of your scalp. It is worth keeping an eye on it.

stock.title: Before you start
stock.intro: Write these down today, with photos and one length measurement you can repeat the same way at week 4 and week 8.
items: Front, sides, crown, back. Pick a method and use the same one every time.
Same light, same angle, same hair state.
Low, medium or high density, and whether strands feel fine, medium or coarse.
Oily, flaky, built up, irritated, or comfortable.
How quickly it dries out, and how easy it is to work with.
Heat, braids, twists, wash-and-gos, and how often you wash.

routine.title: Your routine
routine.intro: One wash day a week. The treatment step is the only part that changes from week to week. The serum is a daily habit, not an extra.

wash.title: Your wash day
steps: Before you get in. Look at your scalp, and split your hair into sections you can actually work through.
Wash the scalp and rinse all the way out.
Bond, protein or lipid, depending on the week. Follow its own label for timing and rinsing; if the product has its own order of steps, that beats this list.
Your conditioner, or the deep conditioner on weeks that call for one.
With conditioner still in and enough slip to get through.
Styler if you use one, and a style that does not need daily redoing.

between.title: Between wash days
groups: Put on your scalp serum, as often as the label says.
Pick a style you can leave alone for a few days.
Notice dryness and tangling before they turn into breakage.
Silk or satin: bonnet, scarf or pillowcase. Every night.
Leave your hair alone. Less handling is the whole point.

weeks.title: What each week is for
weeks.intro: Scalp cleansing and your daily serum stay the same all eight weeks. These are the treatments that move.
items: Your baseline. Moisture wash, deep conditioner, leave-in.
Bring in the ceramide or lipid product.
If your hair has color, bleach, relaxer or heat in its history.
A checkpoint, not an instruction. Take your week 4 photos and length measurement.
A plain moisture-focused wash. Nothing intensive.
Deep conditioning, final photos and measurement, then build your everyday routine from what worked.

use.title: What to use
use.intro: Products by the job they do in this routine. Choose your own brands; these are the jobs to fill.
items: Clears buildup off the skin your hair grows out of.
The step where the growth-focused ingredients go. Core, not a bonus.
Daily, or as the label says
Slip and softness every wash. The step that prevents the most breakage.
The heavier conditioning step, with time to sit.
Keeps the conditioning going between washes.
Puts back the surface lipids that washing and heat wear away.
For hair with color, bleach, relaxer or heat in its history.
Temporarily firms up hair that stretches too easily and snaps.
Week 4, if your hair calls for it
Stops eight hours of friction every night.

choose.title: What you can change, and what you cannot
choose.intro: This plan has growth in the name, so it is worth being straight about which half of it you actually have a say in.
items: Scalp hair grows roughly half an inch a month on average, and the cycles behind it run over months and years. Eight weeks is long enough to build habits and see changes in breakage, comfort and manageability. It is not long enough to judge new growth.
This is the half you control, and it is where most visible length comes from. Less breakage means more of what grew stays on your head.

It is the scalp-care step, and it is a core part of this plan rather than an optional extra. Use it at the frequency its label gives. If a doctor has diagnosed hair loss, a cosmetic serum is not a substitute for the treatment they prescribed.
A decision, not an instruction. If your hair has little heat or chemical history and is not breaking, skip it and condition instead. If you do use it, see how week 5 goes before planning another.

ing.title: What to look for on a label
ing.intro: Scalp ingredients and length-keeping ingredients do different jobs. Both matter here, and they tend to live in different bottles.
items: Studied in lab-grown follicles and dermal papilla cells. Early, interesting, and not proof that a serum regrows hair on a person.
There are human studies, though the quality varies a lot between them. Worth comparing when you choose a serum.
Lipids like the ones hair loses to washing and heat. They condition the surface; they do not act on follicles.
Lubrication and softness. How a product is built matters more than seeing an oil on the list.
Keratin, wheat, rice or silk. They cling to damaged spots and temporarily improve how hair behaves.
Hair holds together with several different kinds of bond, and these products target different ones. Judge the product, not the category.
Behentrimonium compounds, cationic polymers and fatty alcohols. Less friction through a comb means less breakage, which is the whole game here.

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: Look at your cleanser first, then whether anything is sealing the moisture in.
Look at slip, how you detangle, and what your hair rubs against all day.
Look at handling, heat and your chemical history before you buy a treatment.
Buildup, or too many products layered. Clarify, then simplify.
Reduce it or stop it. Do not repeat it automatically.
Product buildup, or too much conditioning. Not a reason to add protein.
Your scalp itches or flakes with a new serum
Stop it and go back to what you had. Try something else in a week or two.

end.title: At the end of eight weeks
notes: Compare your week 8 photos, length and notes with your baseline. Keep the cleansing, conditioning and overnight protection, because that is where retention comes from. Keep the serum if your scalp liked it. Keep protein and bond treatments only if your hair clearly answered them.
If you are losing hair rather than breaking it, or your scalp is sore, inflamed or shedding in patches, that is a dermatologist's question, not a product one.
